title: Central concentration of warm and dense molecular gas in a strongly lensed submillimeter galaxy at z = 6
question: Investigate the physical properties and spatial distribution of warm and dense molecular gas and ionized gas kinematics in the multi-phase ISM of the strongly lensed submillimeter galaxy G09-83808 at z = 6.02.

data.sensitivity: 0.02 Jy beam^-1 km s^-1 in CO(12-11) integrated intensity map; 0.45 mJy/beam per 100 km s^-1 in [O III] 88 um cube; 0.13 mJy/beam per 100 km s^-1 in [N II] 205 um cube

evidence.loc: Lens modeling
evidence.quote: We assume that the mass distribution of the foreground lens galaxy, which is situated at $z=0.776$ (cite: Fudamoto2017), follows a singular isothermal ellipsoid with external shear

what.value: CO(2-1), CO(5-4), and CO(6-5) line observations and fluxes for G09-83808

evidence.loc: Physical properties of highly excited gas
evidence.quote: In the modeling, we incorporate, in addition to the CO(12-11) line detected in this work, the CO(2-1) (Zavala et al. in prep), CO(5-4), and CO(6-5) (cite: Fudamoto2017; Zavala2018) lines detected in G09-83808 (Table [\[COdata\]](#COdata)).

evidence.loc: Physical properties of highly excited gas
evidence.quote: to6pt (1) (cite: Zavala2022), (2) (cite: Zavala2018), (3) (cite: Fudamoto2017).

what.value: Dynamical mass M_dyn = 5 x 10^10 M_sun (including 1 sigma error) and previous redshift z = 6.0269 +/- 0.0006

evidence.loc: Physical properties of highly excited gas
evidence.quote: A constraint that we set is that the molecular gas mass must not exceed the dynamical mass ($M_{\mathrm{dyn}}=5\times 10^{10}\,M_\odot$ including $1\sigma$ error; (cite: Zavala2018)).

evidence.loc: Channel maps of the [O ] 88 um and [N ] 205 um emission
evidence.quote: about $\SI{-100}{km.s^{-1}}$ shift from the previous value ($z=6.0269\pm0.0006$; (cite: Zavala2018)).

what.value: CO(6-5)-normalized CO SLEDs of local starburst galaxies, local AGNs, and average of 4 quasars at 6 < z < 7

evidence.loc: Heating source of CO(12-11) emission
evidence.quote: Figure 8 shows CO(6-5)-normalized CO SLEDs of G09-83808, local starburst galaxies, local AGNs (cite: Mashian2015; Rosenberg2015), and average of 4 quasars at $6<z<7$ (cite: Carniani2019; Li2020).

recipe.goal: Create CO(12-11) channel maps and integrated intensity map, and [O III] 88 um and [N II] 205 um channel maps
recipe.method: Clean channel maps at 100 km s^-1 resolution using the 1.5 mm continuum clean mask, and integrate CO(12-11) over -250 to +250 km s^-1 relative to systemic redshift z = 6.0244.
key_parameters: Spectral resolution = 100 km s^-1, Briggs robust = 2.0, integration range = -250 to +250 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Source-plane reconstruction of CO(12-11) integrated intensity map
recipe.method: Parametric gravitational lens modeling in the cleaned image plane inside the clean mask region with foreground lens parameters fixed from 1.5 mm continuum modeling.
key_parameters: Free parameters: xy-position, total flux Sdv, and effective radius R_e; fixed parameters: Sersic index n = 1, axis ratio q = 0.93, position angle theta_q = 108 deg
assumptions: Foreground lens at z = 0.776 follows a singular isothermal ellipsoid (SIE) with external shear; background source at z = 6.02 has an exponential disk (Sersic n = 1) profile.

recipe.goal: Source-plane reconstruction and kinematic analysis of [O III] 88 um and [N II] 205 um channel maps
recipe.method: Reconstruct individual 100 km s^-1 channel maps in the source plane using circular Gaussian (n = 0.5) or point source models, and fit a single Gaussian to the reconstructed [O III] 88 um line profile to measure systemic redshift.
key_parameters: Sersic index n = 0.5 (circular Gaussian), point source for -200 km s^-1 channel of [N II] 205 um, two circular Gaussian sources for +100 km s^-1 channel of [O III] 88 um
assumptions: Circular Gaussian source profile (n = 0.5) or point source

recipe.goal: Non-LTE radiative transfer modeling of the CO SLED and evaluation of dust attenuation
recipe.method: Two-component 1D non-LTE radiative transfer modeling of galaxy-integrated CO(2-1), CO(5-4), CO(6-5), and CO(12-11) fluxes using RADEX, plus analytical estimation of dust extinction on CO(12-11).
key_parameters: Expanding sphere geometry, dV = 400 km s^-1, background temperature = 19.2 K (CMB at z = 6.02); search ranges: T_kin = 20-700 K, log(n_H2/cm^-3) = 2-6.7, log(N_CO/cm^-2) = 16-20.5
assumptions: Differential magnification across CO transitions is negligible; molecular gas mass <= M_dyn (5 x 10^10 M_sun); L_CO(13-12) < L_CO(12-11) for both components; T_kin,cold < 100 K; dust attenuation model uses lambda_0 = 150 um and beta = 2.5.
